summary: IdP eduPersonScopedAffiliation parser truncates scoped values, resulting in missing RBAC bindings for private VPC users
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that several admin users in their private VPC are seeing 403s when calling the admin routes of the Redwood control plane. Authentication succeeds (SAML assertion is accepted) but the request is treated as unauthenticated for RBAC and falls back to minimal privileges.

Impact:
- ~12 users in Nimbus Health's admin group unable to access control plane admin endpoints (create/modify deployments, view audit logs).
- Production control plane operations for Nimbus are impaired; customer has manual escalation to platform team.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) in prod/us-west.
- Identity Provider: Shibboleth (SAML 2.0).
- Redwood private control plane version: 2025.11.3 (auth-proxy 1.4.2, rbac-syncer 2.0.1).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Log in via SSO as a user in the Nimbus-admin role (example: alice@nimbushealth.org).
2. Call GET /admin/deployments with valid session cookie.
3. Observe 403 and RBAC audit entry showing subject='user:anonymous' or role_bindings=[] .

Observed logs / traces (redacted):
- SAML assertion extracted attributes: eduPersonScopedAffiliation=["member@staff.nimbushealth.org", "employee%40nimbushealth.org@realm"]
- auth-proxy debug: "parsed_affiliations=[\"member\", \"employee%40nimbushealth.org\"]"
- rbac-syncer: "no role bindings found for subject 'employee' (missing domain)"
- application audit: "authorization denied; subject resolved to user:anonymous"

Initial hypothesis:
- The IdP is sending eduPersonScopedAffiliation values that contain an encoded '@' and/or an explicit scoped domain (e.g., user@tenant). Our parser in auth-proxy appears to split on '@' and take the left-hand side only, dropping the tenant portion. Nimbus's role bindings are scoped to the full scoped-affiliation (domain included), so dropping the domain causes a mismatch and no roles are assigned.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- SAML assertion (redacted) attached to ticket (file: saml_assertion_alice_2026-03-09.xml).
- Timeline of affected users (csv).

Immediate customer workaround requested:
- Allowlist affected user certificates for a temporary bypass OR add explicit RBAC user mapping for the truncated username. Customer prefers server-side fix in Redwood to avoid manual mappings for multiple users.

Requested next steps from Support:
- Confirm whether the parser behavior is intended.
- If bug, propose patch for auth-proxy that preserves scoped portion of eduPersonScopedAffiliation when mapping to role bindings OR make mapping configurable.
- Provide short-term mitigation steps customers can apply in private control plane to restore admin access.

investigation_notes: Reproduced locally with auth-proxy 1.4.2 using the provided SAML assertion. Parser used regex /([^@]+)@.*/ and returned only the first capture group. This causes 'employee%40nimbushealth.org@realm' -> 'employee%40nimbushealth.org' then an additional decode step yields 'employee@nimbushealth.org' but subsequent domain-splitting step removes '@nimbushealth.org', leaving 'employee'.
Unit test added: tests/saml_affiliation_parsing_test.rb reproduces the exact failing assertions. Failure triggered when encoded '@' is present inside local part.
rbac-syncer fetches role_bindings by exact-match on subject id (scoped value). Because parser strips scope, lookup fails and fallback to anonymous occurs.
Checked changelog: normalization changes landed in auth-proxy release 1.4.0 (2025-10) that adjusted decoding order. Regression likely introduced during reorder.
provisional_workaround: Create explicit role_bindings for the truncated usernames in customer's private control plane (rbac table) until patch is applied.

Alternatively, configure the identity provider to emit a separate attribute (e.g., edupersonPrincipalName) that maps cleanly to username without encoding; Redwood can be updated to read that attribute if customer prefers.
Support can provide a script to bulk-create role-bindings from the provided CSV of affected users.
next_steps: PR review and CI green: merge fix for auth-proxy to preserve full scoped affiliations (refer to PR #487).
Build and release patched private control plane package (target: 2026-03-16).
Coordinate maintenance window with Nimbus Health for upgrade; provide rollback instructions.
After release, verify affected users can access admin endpoints and confirm role bindings are resolved automatically.
Post-incident: update SSO troubleshooting runbook and add a note about eduPersonScopedAffiliation parsing quirks.
